sanskrit: na hi yogaṃ prapaśyāmi yena mucyeyam āpadaḥ putradāreṇa vā sārdhaṃ prādraveyām anāmayam
english: For I see no means by which I might escape this calamity and flee safely together with my wife and child.

sanskrit: yatitaṃ vai mayā pūrvaṃ yathā tvaṃ vettha brāhmaṇi yataḥ kṣemaṃ tato gantuṃ tvayā tu mama na śrutam
english: I have indeed striven before, as you well know, O Brahmin woman; yet you have not heeded my words about where we might go in safety.

sanskrit: iha jātā vivṛddhāsmi pitā ceha mameti ca uktavaty asi durmedhe yācyamānā mayāsakṛt
english: 'I was born here and grew up here, and my father too is here' — so you have said, O foolish one, even as I beseeched you again and again.

sanskrit: svargato hi pitā vṛddhas tathā mātā ciraṃ tava bāndhavā bhūtapūrvāś ca tatra vāse tu kā ratiḥ
english: Your aged father has gone to heaven, and your mother has long since passed away; your former kinsmen too are gone — what delight then is there in dwelling here?

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ te bandhukāmāyā aśṛṇvantyā vaco mama bandhupraṇāśaḥ saṃprāpto bhṛśaṃ duḥkhakaro mama
english: This ruin of our kin has now come upon you — you who longed for kinship yet would not hear my words — and it brings me the deepest grief.

sanskrit: athavā madvināśo 'yaṃ na hi śakṣyāmi kaṃ cana parityaktum ahaṃ bandhuṃ svayaṃ jīvan nṛśaṃsavat
english: Or rather, this is my own ruin; for I cannot abandon any of my kin of my own accord and live on in cruel indifference.

sanskrit: sahadharmacarīṃ dāntāṃ nityaṃ mātṛsamāṃ mama sakhāyaṃ vihitāṃ devair nityaṃ paramikāṃ gatim
english: She who walks the path of dharma with me, who is self-restrained, who is ever like a mother to me, who was ordained by the gods as my companion and my highest refuge —

sanskrit: mātrā pitrā ca vihitāṃ sadā gārhasthyabhāginīm varayitvā yathānyāyaṃ mantravat pariṇīya ca
english: — she who was appointed by my mother and father to share always in the householder's life, whom I chose according to law and wed with sacred mantras —

sanskrit: kulīnāṃ śīlasaṃpannām apatyajananīṃ mama tvām ahaṃ jīvitasyārthe sādhvīm anapakāriṇīm parityaktuṃ na śakṣyāmi bhāryāṃ nityam anuvratām
english: — this noble and virtuous wife, the mother of my children, who has never done me wrong, who is ever devoted to me — I cannot abandon her to save my own life.

sanskrit: kuta eva parityaktuṃ sutāṃ śakṣyāmy ahaṃ svayam bālām aprāptavayasam ajātavyañjanākṛtim
english: Still less could I abandon my daughter — a mere child, not yet come of age, in whom the marks of womanhood have not yet appeared.

sanskrit: bhartur arthāya nikṣiptāṃ nyāsaṃ dhātrā mahātmanā yasyāṃ dauhitrajāṃl lokān āśaṃse pitṛbhiḥ saha svayam utpādya tāṃ bālāṃ katham utsraṣṭum utsahe
english: She was entrusted to me as a sacred deposit by the great-souled Creator for her future husband's sake; and through her I hope to attain the worlds of my grandsons together with the ancestors. How can I bring myself to abandon this child whom I myself have brought into the world?

sanskrit: manyante ke cid adhikaṃ snehaṃ putre pitur narāḥ kanyāyāṃ naiva tu punar mama tulyāv ubhau matau
english: Some men hold that a father's love for his son is greater than for his daughter; yet in my view both are equal.

sanskrit: yasmiṃl lokāḥ prasūtiś ca sthitā nityam atho sukham apāpāṃ tām ahaṃ bālāṃ katham utsraṣṭum utsahe
english: In her rest the worlds, my lineage, and perpetual happiness. How then can I bring myself to abandon this innocent child?

sanskrit: ātmānam api cotsṛjya tapsye pretavaśaṃ gataḥ tyaktā hy ete mayā vyaktaṃ neha śakṣyanti jīvitum
english: Even if I abandoned myself and passed under the power of the dead, those I left behind could clearly not survive here.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ cānyatamatyāgo nṛśaṃso garhito budhaiḥ ātmatyāge kṛte ceme mariṣyanti mayā vinā
english: The abandonment of any one of these is cruel and condemned by the wise; and if I were to abandon myself, these too would perish without me.

sanskrit: sa kṛcchrām aham āpanno na śaktas tartum āpadam aho dhik kāṃ gatiṃ tv adya gamiṣyāmi sabāndhavaḥ sarvaiḥ saha mṛtaṃ śreyo na tu me jīvitaṃ kṣamam
english: Thus fallen into this terrible strait, I am unable to cross over this calamity. Alas, what course shall I take today? To die together with all my kin would be better; life without them I cannot endure.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca na saṃtāpas tvayā kāryaḥ prākṛteneva karhi cit na hi saṃtāpakālo 'yaṃ vaidyasya tava vidyate
english: The Brahmin woman said: You must not grieve like an ordinary man. This is no time for lamentation; you who know the remedies have no occasion for despair.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ nidhanaṃ sarvair gantavyam iha mānavaiḥ avaśyabhāviny arthe vai saṃtāpo neha vidyate
english: All human beings must inevitably go to their death here; for what is unavoidable, grief serves no purpose.

sanskrit: bhāryā putro 'tha duhitā sarvam ātmārtham iṣyate vyathāṃ jahi subuddhyā tvaṃ svayaṃ yāsyāmi tatra vai
english: Wife, son, and daughter — all are cherished for one's own sake. Cast off your anguish with clear understanding; I myself shall go there.

sanskrit: etad dhi paramaṃ nāryāḥ kāryaṃ loke sanātanam prāṇān api parityajya yad bhartṛhitam ācaret
english: This indeed is the supreme and eternal duty of a woman in the world: that she act for her husband's welfare even at the cost of her own life.

sanskrit: tac ca tatra kṛtaṃ karma tavāpīha sukhāvaham bhavaty amutra cākṣayyaṃ loke 'smiṃś ca yaśaskaram
english: Such a deed done there will bring you happiness even in this world, imperishable reward in the next, and glory in both worlds.

sanskrit: eṣa caiva gurur dharmo yaṃ pravakṣāmy ahaṃ tava arthaś ca tava dharmaś ca bhūyān atra pradṛśyate
english: This is the highest dharma which I shall declare to you; your true purpose and your dharma are both abundantly manifest in this course.

sanskrit: yadartham iṣyate bhāryā prāptaḥ so 'rthas tvayā mayi kanyā caiva kumāraś ca kṛtāham anṛṇā tvayā
english: The purpose for which a wife is desired has been fulfilled in me by you: a daughter and a son have been born, and I have been set free of debt by you.

sanskrit: samarthaḥ poṣaṇe cāsi sutayo rakṣaṇe tathā na tv ahaṃ sutayoḥ śaktā tathā rakṣaṇapoṣaṇe
english: You are capable of nourishing and protecting the two children; I, however, am not equally able to protect and nourish the two of them.

sanskrit: mama hi tvadvihīnāyāḥ sarvakāmā na āpadaḥ kathaṃ syātāṃ sutau bālau bhaveyaṃ ca kathaṃ tv aham
english: For me, bereft of you, all desires would be calamity: how could the two young children fare, and how indeed could I myself fare?

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi vidhavānāthā bālaputrā vinā tvayā mithunaṃ jīvayiṣyāmi sthitā sādhugate pathi
english: How, widowed and helpless, with infant children, without you, shall I sustain the two of us while remaining on the path trodden by the virtuous?

sanskrit: ahaṃkṛtāvaliptaiś ca prārthyamānām imāṃ sutām ayuktais tava saṃbandhe kathaṃ śakṣyāmi rakṣitum
english: With arrogant and insolent men importuning this daughter of mine, men unworthy of alliance with you — how shall I be able to protect her?

sanskrit: utsṛṣṭam āmiṣaṃ bhūmau prārthayanti yathā khagāḥ prārthayanti janāḥ sarve vīrahīnāṃ tathā striyam
english: Just as birds swoop upon flesh thrown to the ground, so all men importune a woman who is without a hero to protect her.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ vicālyamānā vai prārthyamānā durātmabhiḥ sthātuṃ pathi na śakṣyāmi sajjaneṣṭe dvijottama
english: Shaken thus and importuned by wicked men, I shall not be able to remain on the path beloved of the righteous, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: kathaṃ tava kulasyaikām imāṃ bālām asaṃskṛtām pitṛpaitāmahe mārge niyoktum aham utsahe
english: How can I bring myself to set this solitary, unformed girl of your lineage on the path of her fathers and grandfathers?

sanskrit: kathaṃ śakṣyāmi bāle 'smin guṇān ādhātum īpṣitān anāthe sarvato lupte yathā tvaṃ dharmadarśivān
english: How shall I be able to instil in this child the virtues that are desired, she who is helpless and abandoned on all sides — as you, who perceive dharma, could have done?

sanskrit: imām api ca te bālām anāthāṃ paribhūya mām anarhāḥ prārthayiṣyanti śūdrā vedaśrutiṃ yathā
english: Disregarding me and treating this orphaned girl of yours with contempt, unworthy men will importune her — as Śūdras importune the hearing of the Veda.

sanskrit: tāṃ ced ahaṃ na ditseyaṃ tvadguṇair upabṛṃhitām pramathyaināṃ hareyus te havir dhvāṅkṣā ivādhvarāt
english: And if I were to refuse to give her away, one endowed with your virtues, those men would violently carry her off, as crows snatch the oblation from a sacrifice.

sanskrit: saṃprekṣamāṇā putraṃ te nānurūpam ivātmanaḥ anarhavaśam āpannām imāṃ cāpi sutāṃ tava
english: Watching your son, who seems unworthy even of me, and this daughter of yours as well fallen into the power of the unworthy —

sanskrit: avajñātā ca lokasya tathātmānam ajānatī avaliptair narair brahman mariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ
english: — scorned by the world, not knowing what I myself am worth, at the hands of insolent men, O Brahmin, I shall surely die. There is no doubt of this.

sanskrit: tau vihīnau mayā bālau tvayā caiva mamātmajau vinaśyetāṃ na saṃdeho matsyāv iva jalakṣaye
english: Those two children of mine, bereft of me and of you, would perish without doubt — like two fish when their water dries up.

sanskrit: tritayaṃ sarvathāpy evaṃ vinaśiṣyaty asaṃśayam tvayā vihīnaṃ tasmāt tvaṃ māṃ parityaktum arhasi
english: All three of us will surely perish in every way, bereft of you. Therefore you ought to abandon me.

sanskrit: vyuṣṭir eṣā parā strīṇāṃ pūrvaṃ bhartuḥ parā gatiḥ na tu brāhmaṇa putrāṇāṃ viṣaye parivartitum
english: This is the highest fulfilment for women: that the husband's welfare comes first and is the highest goal; but not, O Brahmin, to remain spinning in the domain of one's sons.

sanskrit: parityaktaḥ sutaś cāyaṃ duhiteyaṃ tathā mayā bāndhavāś ca parityaktās tvadarthaṃ jīvitaṃ ca me
english: This son has been forsaken by me, and this daughter likewise; kinsmen too have been forsaken, and my very life — all for your sake.

sanskrit: yajñais tapobhir niyamair dānaiś ca vividhais tathā viśiṣyate striyā bhartur nityaṃ priyahite sthitiḥ
english: Over sacrifices, austerities, observances, and various acts of giving, a woman's constant devotion to the welfare and happiness of her husband is far superior.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ yac cikīrṣāmi dharmyaṃ paramasaṃmatam iṣṭaṃ caiva hitaṃ caiva tava caiva kulasya ca
english: That which I am about to do is righteous and supremely approved; it is what is desired and beneficial — for you and for your lineage alike.

sanskrit: iṣṭāni cāpy apatyāni dravyāṇi suhṛdaḥ priyāḥ āpaddharmavimokṣāya bhāryā cāpi satāṃmatam
english: Even children dear to one, one's wealth, cherished friends — and even a wife — may be given up, according to the opinion of the good, to secure release by the law in times of calamity.

sanskrit: ekato vā kulaṃ kṛtsnam ātmā vā kulavardhana na samaṃ sarvam eveti budhānām eṣa niścayaḥ
english: On one side the entire lineage, on the other a single self, O increaser of the family — the wise have firmly concluded that all the rest together are not equal to the self.

sanskrit: sa kuruṣva mayā kāryaṃ tārayātmānam ātmanā anujānīhi mām ārya sutau me parirakṣa ca
english: Therefore, act together with me in what must be done; save yourself by yourself. Give me leave, O noble one, and protect our two children.

sanskrit: avadhyāḥ striya ity āhur dharmajñā dharmaniścaye dharmajñān rākṣasān āhur na hanyāt sa ca mām api
english: Those who know dharma say in their determination of dharma that women must not be killed; and they call rakshasas knowers of dharma — so he should not kill me either.

sanskrit: niḥsaṃśayo vadhaḥ puṃsāṃ strīṇāṃ saṃśayito vadhaḥ ato mām eva dharmajña prasthāpayitum arhasi
english: The killing of a man is certain; the killing of a woman is uncertain. Therefore, O knower of dharma, you ought to send me instead.

sanskrit: bhuktaṃ priyāṇy avāptāni dharmaś ca carito mayā tvatprasūtiḥ priyā prāptā na māṃ tapsyaty ajīvitam
english: I have enjoyed pleasant things and obtained what I desired; I have lived according to dharma; I have gained the cherished fruit of being born of you. I shall not grieve at death.

sanskrit: jātaputrā ca vṛddhā ca priyakāmā ca te sadā samīkṣyaitad ahaṃ sarvaṃ vyavasāyaṃ karomy ataḥ
english: I am one who has borne a son, who is mature, and who has always sought your happiness. Considering all this, I now resolve upon this course.

sanskrit: utsṛjyāpi ca mām ārya vetsyasy anyām api striyam tataḥ pratiṣṭhito dharmo bhaviṣyati punas tava
english: Even when you have let me go, O noble one, you will take another wife; and thus your dharma will again be established.

sanskrit: na cāpy adharmaḥ kalyāṇa bahupatnīkatā nṛṇām strīṇām adharmaḥ sumahān bhartuḥ pūrvasya laṅghane
english: Nor is it adharma for men to have many wives, O auspicious one; but for women the adharma is very great in transgressing against a prior husband.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ samīkṣya tvam ātmatyāgaṃ ca garhitam ātmānaṃ tāraya mayā kulaṃ cemau ca dārakau
english: Considering all this, and that self-destruction is condemned, save yourself through me; and save the lineage and these two children.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tayā bhartā tāṃ samāliṅgya bhārata mumoca bāṣpaṃ śanakaiḥ sabhāryo bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by her, the husband, O Bhārata, embraced her and, together with his wife, slowly shed tears, deeply afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tayor duḥkhitayor vākyam atimātraṃ niśamya tat bhṛśaṃ duḥkhaparītāṅgī kanyā tāv abhyabhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those excessively sorrowful words of the two grief-stricken ones, the daughter, whose limbs were overwhelmed with intense grief, spoke to them both.

sanskrit: kim idaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhārtau roravītho anāthavat mamāpi śrūyatāṃ kiṃ cic chrutvā ca kriyatāṃ kṣamam
english: Why do you two, so deeply afflicted with grief, cry out like those who are helpless? Let something of mine be heard as well; and having heard it, do what is fit.

sanskrit: dharmato 'haṃ parityājyā yuvayor nātra saṃśayaḥ tyaktavyāṃ māṃ parityajya trātaṃ sarvaṃ mayaikayā
english: By dharma I am the one to be abandoned by the two of you — there is no doubt in this. Abandon me, she who is fit to be abandoned, and everything will be saved by me alone.

sanskrit: ity artham iṣyate 'patyaṃ tārayiṣyati mām iti tasminn upasthite kāle tarataṃ plavavan mayā
english: For this very reason offspring are desired — 'it will save me,' one thinks. Now that this occasion has arrived, use me as a raft to cross over.

sanskrit: iha vā tārayed durgād uta vā pretya tārayet sarvathā tārayet putraḥ putra ity ucyate budhaiḥ
english: Whether one saves from a danger here in this life or saves after death in the next — in every way a son saves; that is why the wise call him 'putra' (son, saviour).

sanskrit: ākāṅkṣante ca dauhitrān api nityaṃ pitāmahāḥ tān svayaṃ vai paritrāsye rakṣantī jīvitaṃ pituḥ
english: Grandfathers also always long for their daughter's sons; I shall myself rescue them by protecting my father's life.

sanskrit: bhrātā ca mama bālo 'yaṃ gate lokam amuṃ tvayi acireṇaiva kālena vinaśyeta na saṃśayaḥ
english: And this little brother of mine — if you, father, were to pass to yonder world, he would surely perish within no long time. There is no doubt of this.

sanskrit: tāte 'pi hi gate svargaṃ vinaṣṭe ca mamānuje piṇḍaḥ pitṝṇāṃ vyucchidyet tat teṣām apriyaṃ bhavet
english: For if father goes to heaven and my younger brother also perishes, the ancestral oblations would be cut off — and that would be displeasing to them.

sanskrit: pitrā tyaktā tathā mātrā bhrātrā cāham asaṃśayam duḥkhād duḥkhataraṃ prāpya mriyeyam atathocitā
english: Abandoned by my father, and likewise by my mother, and by my brother, there is no doubt that I, not accustomed to such, would die, having fallen into a grief worse than grief.

sanskrit: tvayi tv aroge nirmukte mātā bhrātā ca me śiśuḥ saṃtānaś caiva piṇḍaś ca pratiṣṭhāsyaty asaṃśayam
english: But if you are safely delivered, unharmed, then my mother, my young brother, the continuation of the lineage, and the ancestral oblations will all without doubt be established.

sanskrit: ātmā putraḥ sakhā bhāryā kṛcchraṃ tu duhitā kila sa kṛcchrān mocayātmānaṃ māṃ ca dharmeṇa yojaya
english: Oneself, one's son, a friend — that is a wife; a daughter is truly a burden, so they say. Therefore, free yourself from this burden and assign me to dharma.

sanskrit: anāthā kṛpaṇā bālā yatrakvacanagāminī bhaviṣyāmi tvayā tāta vihīnā kṛpaṇā bata
english: Helpless, pitiable, a child, wandering wherever I may — I shall be wretched without you, father. Alas, how pitiable!

sanskrit: athavāhaṃ kariṣyāmi kulasyāsya vimokṣaṇam phalasaṃsthā bhaviṣyāmi kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
english: Or rather, I shall achieve the liberation of this family; I shall have attained the fruit of my existence by performing this most difficult deed.

sanskrit: athavā yāsyase tatra tyaktvā māṃ dvijasattama pīḍitāhaṃ bhaviṣyāmi tad avekṣasva mām api
english: Or if you go there leaving me behind, O best of twice-born, I shall be afflicted — consider me as well in this.

sanskrit: tad asmadarthaṃ dharmārthaṃ prasavārthaṃ ca sattama ātmānaṃ parirakṣasva tyaktavyāṃ māṃ ca saṃtyaja
english: Therefore, for our sake, for the sake of dharma, and for the sake of progeny, O virtuous one, protect yourself; and abandon me, who am fit to be abandoned.

sanskrit: avaśyakaraṇīye 'rthe mā tvāṃ kālo 'tyagād ayam tvayā dattena toyena bhaviṣyati hitaṃ ca me
english: In this matter which must inevitably be done, let not this moment pass you by. The water-oblation given by you will be of benefit to me.

sanskrit: kiṃ nv ataḥ paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ yad vayaṃ svargate tvayi yācamānāḥ parād annaṃ paridhāvemahi śvavat
english: What greater grief could there be than this — that we, with you gone to heaven, should run about begging food from others like dogs?

sanskrit: tvayi tv aroge nirmukte kleśād asmāt sabāndhave amṛte vasatī loke bhaviṣyāmi sukhānvitā
english: But if you are delivered safely, unharmed, from this affliction, with your kinsmen alive, I, dwelling in this world, shall be filled with happiness.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ tasyā niśamya paridevitam pitā mātā ca sā caiva kanyā prarurudus trayaḥ
english: Hearing her lamentation of many kinds, the father, the mother, and the daughter herself all three wept aloud.

sanskrit: tataḥ praruditān sarvān niśamyātha sutas tayoḥ utphullanayano bālaḥ kalam avyaktam abravīt
english: Then, hearing all of them weeping, the young son of the two of them, a mere boy with wide-open eyes, spoke softly in indistinct words.

sanskrit: mā rodīs tāta mā mātar mā svasas tvam iti bruvan prahasann iva sarvāṃs tān ekaikaṃ so 'pasarpati
english: Saying 'Do not weep, father; do not weep, mother; do not weep, sister,' he approached them one by one, seeming almost to smile.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tṛṇam ādāya prahṛṣṭaḥ punar abravīt anena taṃ haniṣyāmi rākṣasaṃ puruṣādakam
english: Then he picked up a blade of grass and, joyful, spoke again: 'With this I shall slay that man-eating Rākṣasa!'

sanskrit: tathāpi teṣāṃ duḥkhena parītānāṃ niśamya tat bālasya vākyam avyaktaṃ harṣaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: Even so, hearing those indistinct words of the child, great joy arose among them who were overcome with grief.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kāla iti jñātvā kuntī samupasṛtya tān gatāsūn amṛteneva jīvayantīdam abravīt
english: Recognizing that the moment had come, Kuntī approached them — as if reviving those at the point of death with nectar — and spoke these words.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca kutomūlam idaṃ duḥkhaṃ jñātum icchāmi tattvataḥ viditvā apakarṣeyaṃ śakyaṃ ced apakarṣitum
english: Kuntī said: I wish to know the root cause of this grief in truth; and having known it, I would remove it, if it can indeed be removed.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca upapannaṃ satām etad yad bravīṣi tapodhane na tu duḥkham idaṃ śakyaṃ mānuṣeṇa vyapohitum
english: The Brahmin said: What you say, O rich in austerity, is fitting for those who are good; yet this grief cannot be dispelled by a human being.

sanskrit: samīpe nagarasyāsya bako vasati rākṣasaḥ īśo janapadasyāsya purasya ca mahābalaḥ
english: Near this city there lives a Rākṣasa named Baka, who is the lord of this countryside and of this town, and who is of great might.

sanskrit: puṣṭo mānuṣamāṃsena durbuddhiḥ puruṣādakaḥ rakṣaty asurarāṇ nityam imaṃ janapadaṃ balī
english: Nourished on human flesh, evil-minded, a devourer of men, this powerful one perpetually protects this countryside from other demons.
